channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Indian Rupee ticks lower due to higher US bond Yields
item.description: The Indian Rupee (INR) drops against the US Dollar (USD) on Thursday. The USD/INR pair edges down to near 95.60, with the Indian currency facing a tough fight against higher United States (US) Treasury Yields.

item.title: BoE interest rate seen on hold as markets await guidance from Bailey
item.description: The Bank of England (BoE) is on track to keep the benchmark Bank Rate steady at 3.75% for the fifth straight meeting on Thursday, despite the renewed surge in Oil prices in July and a leadership change in the United Kingdom (UK).

item.title: British Pound: BoE policy seen on extended hold – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale strategists analyzes- the Bank of England’s (BoE) upcoming meeting, expecting Bank Rate to remain at 3.75% with some hawkish dissent. They note easing inflation expectations and a loosening labour market, but also higher energy prices and government income support.

item.title: US Dollar: Post-FOMC losses likely to remain limited – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities strategists note that the US Dollar (USD) weakened after the July Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) rate hold and Chair Warsh’s lack of hawkish guidance.

item.title: Bank of England: Market pricing stays hawkish – ING
item.description: ING’s Michiel Tukker and Padhraic Garvey expect no change in the Bank of England (BoE) policy rate at the upcoming meeting, despite markets pricing in substantial tightening.

item.title: British Pound: Fiscal concerns may weigh on Sterling – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank Senior FX Strategist Jane Foley discusses GBP/USD following the latest Federal Reserve (Fed) decision and ahead of the Bank of England (BoE) meeting. She expects GBP/USD to trade around 1.32–1.33 over the next one to three months.

item.title: Silver price today: Silver falls, according to FXStreet data
item.description: Silver prices (XAG/USD) fell on Thursday, according to FXStreet data. Silver trades at $57.79 per troy ounce, down 0.25% from the $57.94 it cost on Wednesday.

item.title: Japanese Yen: BoJ tone could lift JPY against US Dollar – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Volkmar Baur expects the Bank of Japan to keep its overnight call rate unchanged, as fully priced by markets. The focus is on guidance, with inflation around 2% and leading indicators pointing higher.

item.title: Euro steadies near weekly highs following bright Eurozone growth numbers
item.description: The Euro (EUR) is retracing previous losses against the US Dollar (USD) on Wednesday, fuelled by upbeat Eurozone Gross Domestic Product (GDP) and economic confidence data.

item.title: Japan PM Takaichi: Will avoid debt channel to ensure market trust
item.description: Japan Prime Minister (PM) Sanae Takaichi said during the European trading session on Thursday that the government won’t lean on debt funds to supplement temporary tax cuts, in an attempt to maintain market trust.

item.title: Federal Reserve: Dollar awaits clearer policy signals - Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale’s Jan Groen reviews the July 2026 Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) outcome, noting the Federal Reserve (Fed) left the Fed funds target range at 3.5%-3.75% and signaled a cautious stance on inflation.

item.title: Euro rebounds strongly against Yen after German, Eurozone Q2 GDP data
item.description: The Euro (EUR) claws back its early losses and turns almost flat against the Japanese Yen (JPY) after the release of preliminary German Q2 Gross Domestic Product (GDP) and inflation data for its six states.

item.title: Canadian Dollar edges lower amid rebounding USD as traders await key US macro data
item.description: The USD/CAD pair attracts some buyers on Thursday and, for now, seems to have snapped a two-day losing streak to a more than one-week low, around the 1.4025-1.4020 area touched the previous day.

item.title: Eurozone GDP returns to growth in Q2, rises strongly by 0.4%
item.description: According to Eurostat, Eurozone Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth turns positive in the second quarter of this year after declining 0.2% in the previous quarter. The GDP growth data is at 0.4%, higher than estimates of 0.2%.

item.title: US Dollar: Fed reaction function clouds dollar outlook – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Derek Halpenny says the Fed’s decision to hold rates, combined with Chair Warsh’s unclear justification, steepened the Treasury curve and weakened the dollar. Rising inflation expectations and concerns over Federal Reserve (Fed) credibility now point to further depreciation risk.

item.title: Swiss Franc: Undervaluation supports APAC recovery trades – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Geoff Yu highlights that the Swiss Franc looks undervalued on both nominal and real effective exchange rate measures, near one-year and 15‑month lows respectively.

item.title: GBP/USD Price Forecast: Keeps the red near 1.3350 as traders await BoE rate decision
item.description: The GBP/USD pair meets with fresh supply on Thursday and retreats further from the weekly high, around the 1.3385-1.3390 region, touched the previous day.

item.title: Euro: Data-driven range trade into Q3 against US Dollar – ING
item.description: Chris Turner at ING writes that EUR/USD bounced modestly after the FOMC but was constrained by higher long-dated US yields and pressure on US growth stocks.

item.title: US GDP expected to grow at 2.1% in Q2, unshaken by Iran conflict
item.description: The United States (US) Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) is set to publish its preliminary estimate of second-quarter Gross Domestic Product (GDP) on Thursday, with analysts expecting the data to show annualised growth at a solid 2.1%, a modest cooling from the 2.1% expansion recorded in the previou

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD turns upside down amid soaring US Treasury Yields
item.description: Silver price (XAG/USD) gives back its early gains and turns negative on Thursday. The white metal trades 0.7% lower at around $57.25 in the European trade after a positive start, which led to hitting an intraday high at $58.65.

item.title: Indian Rupee: RBI seen on hold as growth solid – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s analysts report that USD/INR has eased as India’s June industrial production surprised to the upside and inflation stayed within the Reserve Bank of India’s target band.

item.title: Federal Reserve: Extended pause with 2027 cuts – UOB
item.description: UOB’s Suan Teck Kin and Alvin Liew analyze the latest FOMC decision, noting the Fed Funds Target Rate remains at 3.50%-3.75% for a fifth straight meeting despite three dissenting votes favoring a hike.

item.title: Gold bears retain control as USD strengthens on Fed hike bets and Mideast crisis
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) maintains its offered tone through the first half of the European session on Thursday and seems vulnerable to following an intraday rejection near the $4,100 mark.

item.title: German flash Q2 GDP rises 0.2% QoQ, beats 0.1% estimates
item.description: German preliminary Q2 Gross Domestic Product (GDP) rises at a 0.2% pace, beating the estimates of 0.1%, according to the Federal Statistics Office of Germany. However, the GDP growth remains slower than the previous reading of 0.3%.

item.title: Swiss Franc retreats further despite bright KOF Leading Indicators data
item.description: The Swiss Franc (CHF) remains on the defensive against the US Dollar (USD) Thursday despite the unexpected improvement of Swiss leading indicators.

item.title: US Dollar Index Price Forecast: Rebounds to near 101.00 as bullish bias prevails
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY), which measures the value of the US Dollar (USD) against six major currencies, is gaining ground after two days of losses and trading around 101.00 during the European hours on Thursday.

item.title: British Pound: BoE hike pricing supports Sterling against US Dollar – MUFG
item.description: MUFG's Derek Halpenny notes that the British Pound (GBP) has been the strongest G10 currency after the US Dollar (USD) since the Middle East conflict began, with attention now on the Bank of England’s (BoE) July decision.

item.title: Australian Dollar stays on the defensive against a broadly firmer USD, ahead of US data
item.description: The AUD/USD pair struggles to capitalize on the previous day's late rebound from the 0.6920 region, or an over two-week low, and seesaws between tepid gains/minor losses through the early European session on Thursday.

item.title: Equities: Fed-driven yield spike pressures equities – Deutsche Bank
item.description: Deutsche Bank notes that the Federal Reserve’s (Fed) on-hold decision and limited detail from Chair Warsh sparked a sharp steepening in the Treasury curve, pushing the 30-year yield to 5.20% and weighing on equities.

item.title: WTI Oil extends gains beyond $84.00 as US resumes strikes in Iran
item.description: Oil prices have risen about 7% over the last two days, pushing the price of the US benchmark West Texas Intermediate (WTI) barrel to levels above $84.00 on Thursday, up from the $77.16 lows seen earlier in the week.
